_note: Release Train v2 merge freeze (AGENTS.md section 25.3; docs/ops/RELEASE_TRAIN_MERGE_FREEZE.md). Read by scripts/lib/release_train_freeze.py. The window schedule is config/release_train_policy.json windows[] (days included); this file only says how the freeze is applied around it. starts_min_before_window mirrors the delegation's merge_freeze block; the host uses the larger of the two when the delegation is readable. request_grace_min must equal config/release_train_n8n.json grace_min: a window with no request by then was skipped (no catch-up), so its freeze ends. ci_lead_min: GitHub's scheduled sweep is best effort, so the CI status turns pending this many minutes before a freeze starts. stale_after_min: a train still ACKNOWLEDGED that long after its window, or a live train whose state has not moved that long, stops freezing and raises a P1 (reconcile it with train-orphan-resolve / reconcile). train_pr_authors: a train/<id> batch PR is exempt only when its author is listed; tradeai-release-train[bot] is the App's bot login, read from the public author of the App's batch PR #2069 (no host config read). An empty list exempts nothing. On the host the batch PR's train id must also be a live train in <state>/trains. operator_logins: the freeze-exempt label counts only when the login that applied it (the PR's labeled event) is listed; the agent merge helper never honours the label. PatsKiller is also the identity agents use with gh, so the label is not agent-proof: the host check-pr is the real gate against agents (docs/ops/RELEASE_TRAIN_MERGE_FREEZE.md section 6).
